Commissioner Apodaca called the special hybrid meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the
Norwalk City Hall, Council Chambers and via video/teleconference pursuant to the
provisions of Assembly Bill 361. Responding to roll call in person was Commissioner
Apodaca, and via Zoom, Commissioner Garcia, Commissioner Navas and Vice Chair
Lopez. Chair Barragan was absent. Also present were John P. Ramirez, Director of
Community Development, Gloria V. Ramirez, Deputy City Attorney; Jill Ann Arabe,
Development Services Manager, Gabriel R. Salazar, Senior Planner; Andrew Arellano,
Assistant Planner; and Ruth Hoffmann, Administrative Secretary.

MEETING MINUTES

The Planning Commission approved the minutes of the Special Meeting of September
13, 2023.

CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 2023-03
DIRECTOR APPROVAL REQUEST NO. 2023-08
Crystal Cyprian and Joy Cyprian, Joy’s Children’s Learning Center (“Applicant”); a
request to permit a child care facility within an existing 2,785 square foot building and
2,797 square foot building for ancillary storage on a 0.37 acre site. The subject property
is generally known as 11004 Adoree Street, located on the southeast corner of Adoree
Street and Studebaker Road (also known as Assessor’s Parcel Number (“APN”) 8050-
026-001), in the Commercial and Office (C and O) zone. The project includes a request
for:
(1) Conditional Use Permit: To permit a child care facility within an existing 2,785
  square foot single-story building; and
(2) Director Approval Request No. 2023-08: To allow an eighteen (18) percent
  reduction (three spaces) from the required number of parking spaces.
(3) Environmental: Consider and find the project exempt from California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities).

Commissioner Apodaca opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Senior Planner Salazar
presented a detailed report stating that the item before the Commission is a request to
permit a child care facility within an existing 2,785 square foot building and a 2,797
square foot building for ancillary storage, as well as allow an 18 percent reduction (three
parking spaces) from the required number of parking spaces; that the following safety
mechanisms are proposed and conditioned to minimize any potential vehicle congestion
generated by the use: that parents are required to accompany their children into the
building and sign them in and out; that the enrollment be limited to a maximum of twenty
(20) children; that a staggered drop off schedule with children arriving from 7:00 a.m. to
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 2

10:30 a.m. in fifteen minute increments with a maximum of two children in each block
of time; that one on-site traffic monitor will be outside and in the parking lot to control
vehicles parking safely and leaving the site in an orderly manner; that two designated
parking spaces are required for drop-off and pick-up; and that security cameras be
placed strategically around the site.

Further, Senior Planner Salazar indicated that based upon the study and with the
recommended conditions, the project would have sufficient parking to accommodate
the use; that staff has added Condition No. 4 which states that within six months and
one year of commencement of use, staff shall review the use for compliance with
conditions of approval and for evaluation of site circulation and related vehicle/traffic
impacts surrounding the subject site; that a report of the six-month and one-year
evaluation shall be provided to the Planning Commission for further consideration of
conditions of approval and continuation of use; that at that time, the City may require
the applicant to construct appropriate site improvements including a drive-through lane
along the north side of the property or to the east side of the building, as feasible, to
address potential site circulation issues.

Senior Planner Salazar shared that, in closing, staff believes that the proposed project
will enhance the surrounding area by revitalizing a vacant site and providing a local-
serving commercial use compatible with the neighborhood; that the project complies
with applicable City codes, and based upon a trip generation and parking study,
including the recommended conditions of approval, it provides adequate parking and
vehicular circulation and is consistent with the General Plan by providing adequate child
care services for the needs of the community; and that it is staff’s recommendation that
the Commission: (1) adopt Resolution No. 23-26 to approve Conditional Use Permit No.
2023-03 subject to the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and (2) adopt
Resolution No 23-27 to approve Director Approval Request No. 2023-08 subject to the
conditions of approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and (3) consider and find the project
exempt from CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15301 (Existing Facilities).

Commissioner Apodaca commented on Condition No. 4 that makes reference to a six-
month and a one-year review period for compliance with the conditions of approval and
for evaluation of site circulation and related vehicle/traffic impacts surrounding the
subject site, and she asked what will constitute further site improvements.

Director Ramirez stated that staff would work with Public Safety and look at the severity
of traffic impacts.

The applicant, Joy Cyprian introduced her daughter Crystal, and she stated that they
are the owners and founders of Joy’s Children’s Learning Center; that they both hold a
Masters Degree in Child Development; that regarding Condition No. 4 they believe that
this is excessive; that they ran and owned a number of child care facilities and never
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 3

had an issue as they learned how to stagger schedules and never had a problem with
traffic in 30 years. Ms. Cyprian asked that Condition No. 4 be modified as the cost of
implementing site improvements as outlined in this condition would be excessive.

Ben Shen, of the ownership group, indicated that truck traffic or collisions have not been
an issue at the site; that Adoree Street is very safe, especially in the mornings; that the
staggered drop-off will not bring in additional traffic; that the sticking point is with
Condition No. 4; that one of the options is to take away the grass area used as a
playground, which would not work; that the property has just been renovated and to
demolish a part of it is not feasible; that should a traffic problem arise, they would like
to work with the City to solve the problem.

Ms. Cyprian indicated that they had a meeting in February with the Planning staff
because they wanted to address parking; that staff did not see any issues at that time;
that, as requested, they provided a parking study; and that they were a bit blind-sided
by Condition No. 4. She thanked the Commission for hearing their concerns and she
asked that they take their request under consideration.

Director Ramirez shared that they did receive an application in February; that they
worked with the applicant and property owner in understanding the flow of traffic and
parking components of it, and asked for additional information. Further, he indicated
that there have been about nine accidents across the street from the subject site.

Deputy City Attorney Ramirez commented on Condition No. 4, and she indicated that
there are mechanisms that would allow the City to review, in half a year and in one year,
the use for compliance with conditions of approval and for evaluation of site circulation
and related vehicle/traffic impacts surrounding the subject site.

Since there were no other persons wishing to present testimony, Commissioner
Apodaca closed the public hearing.

Commissioner Apodaca stated that she is very concerned about that location because
of the traffic flow; that she is familiar with how parents drop off their children; and that
she believes that Condition No. 4 is definitely appropriate.

Commissioner Garcia indicated that he has a concern with that area as being very busy;
and that, other than that, he agrees with the half a year and one year condition.

Vice Chair Lopez shared that she has the same concerns with traffic as expressed by
her fellow Commissioners.

Commissioner Navas stated that he, too, has similar concerns with the entrance being
off Studebaker Road; that while he understands where the applicant is coming from,
staff is making a reasonable request; and that he is in favor of Condition No. 4.

After reopening the public hearing to allow Mr. Shen to provide an additional comment,
he shared that accidents are mainly caused by late night traffic; that Adoree is
completely on the other side of the street; that they are not requesting that Condition
No. 4 be removed but that the wording be modified to indicate that if there are issues
there will be other options to address that concern.

Deputy City Attorney Ramirez suggested that a part of the condition could be modified
by stating that, at that time, the City may require the applicant to construct appropriate
improvements which could include the words “but not limited to” the site improvements
contained in Condition No. 4 as this would allow the City some flexibility.

Commissioner Apodaca stated that she is aware that most of the accidents occur to the
north of the property; however, she has serious concerns with that site being a day care
facility.

It was moved by Commissioner Apodaca and seconded by Vice Chair Lopez to direct
staff to prepare resolutions for Planning Commission consideration to deny Conditional
Use Permit No. 2023-03 and Director Approval Request No. 2023-08.

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO.
  2023-03 WITH CONDITIONS AND FINDING THAT THE PROJECT IS
  EXEMPT UNDER CEQA § 15301 (EXISTING FACILITIES)

  WHEREAS, Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No. 2023-03 was submitted by Crystal and Joy
Cyprian, Joy’s Children Learning Center, for 11004 Adoree Street (“Subject Property”); also
known as Assessor’s Parcel Number (“APN”) 8056-026-001, a request to permit a childcare
facility on a 0.37-acre site; and

  WHEREAS, Director Approval Request (DAR) No. 2023-08 was filed in conjunction with
this request; and

  WHEREAS, Sections 17.04.190 and 17.11.010 of the Norwalk Municipal Code require the
review and approval of a conditional use permit by the Planning Commission of the City of Norwalk
("Planning Commission”) for a childcare facility; and

  WHEREAS, the purpose and intent of requiring a conditional use permit is to ensure that
compatibility is maintained between a conditional use on a specific site, and other existing and
future land uses on adjacent and surrounding properties; and

  WHEREAS, pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”), this project
will not have a significant effect on the environment and is listed as a Class 1 (Existing Facilities)
Categorical Exemption, Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations, Section 15301. Class 1
Exemption consists of the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, or minor alteration
of existing public or private facilities, mechanical equipment, or topographical features, involving
negligible or no expansion of existing or former use; and

  WHEREAS, Section 17.02.210.A of the Norwalk Municipal Code authorizes the Planning
Commission to grant a conditional use permit and impose such conditions as it deems necessary
and reasonable to protect the best interests of the surrounding property or neighborhood and to
ensure compliance with the Zoning Ordinance and the General Plan; and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission conducted a duly noticed public hearing on
October 11, 2023, to consider CUP No. 2023-03, at which time oral and documentary evidence
related to the application were received.

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. The foregoing recitals are true and correct and are hereby incorporated as
substantive findings in the Resolution.

  Section 2. The Planning Commission finds and determines that the degree of
compatibility required by the Zoning Ordinance will be maintained with respect to the use of the
site as a childcare facility, considering other existing and potential uses within the general area,
with the incorporation of recommended conditions of approval. The childcare use provides
neighborhood services similar to other office and commercial uses.
   Section 3.  The proposed use will not be detrimental to the public health, safety, and
welfare or adversely affect property values or the present and future development of the
surrounding area with the incorporation of the suggested conditions of approval. The proposed
childcare facility will have a positive impact on the surrounding neighborhood. It will revitalize a
vacant, underutilized site and improve the vitality of the site by providing a much-needed service
to the community.

  Section 4. The proposed use is consistent with the policies and objectives of the Norwalk
General Plan to provide for adequate childcare facilities to meet the needs of today’s working
community, encourage the development of childcare facilities within the city, and encourage the
maintenance and enhancement of areas for creation of a positive image for Norwalk. The project
will revitalize a vacant site, provide local services to the community, and enhance the surrounding
area. The trip generation and parking demand study prepared for the project demonstrates
minimal impacts are anticipated to the surrounding neighborhood.

  Section 5. The Planning Commission finds that the proposed project is exempt from
CEQA under Section 15301 (Existing Facilities) because the proposed use is within an existing
building and will involve no expansion.

  Section 6. The Planning Commission does hereby approve Conditional Use Permit No.
2023-03 subject to the Conditions of Approval in attached Exhibit "A."

  APPROVED AND ADOPTED BY THE NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION on this
11th day of October 2023.

The following Conditions of Approval shall be incorporated into all applicable final construction
plans and a copy of these conditions shall be placed on the first sheet of the final building plans:

1. The site plan and floor plan received and dated September 11, 2023, shall be approved.

2. The use shall comply with the following:

  c. Parents and/or guardians shall accompany their children into the building and sign them

  e. Two employees shall be available at all times to assist and facilitate morning drop-offs and
  afternoon pick-ups.
  f. No parking is allowed in the residential area along Adoree Street and no parking along
  Studebaker Road.
  g. The hours of operation for the childcare facility shall be Monday through Friday, from 6:30
  a.m. to 6:30 p.m.
  h. The surveillance camera system is to be maintained operational at all times, including
  during non-business hours. The system features and functions shall be accessible by
  business management staff at all times during normal business hours. The system shall
  provide a video feed of sufficient quality to permit the Public Safety Department and
  Norwalk Sheriff Station to utilize the feed for law enforcement purposes, whether
  emergency or investigatory. Business shall ensure all video recordings/feeds remain
  accessible on a Digital Video Recording system for a minimum of 30 days.

  a. A surveillance camera system plan (Verkada) shall be submitted for review and approval
  by the Departments of Public Safety and Community Development. Surveillance cameras
  shall be placed in a position to provide visual coverage of the parking lot, adjacent streets,
  and building entrances.
  b. All infrastructure necessary to serve the proposed development (water, sewer, storm
  drain, and street improvements) shall be in operation. (Engineering)

  evaluation shall be provided to the Planning Commission for further consideration of

  to construct appropriate site improvements including a drive-through lane along the north side

Section 17.02.290.D requires a written recommendation of approval by the Planning

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

The Automobile Parking (P) zone was adopted by Ordinance No. 114 in 1959 with the
intent to serve as setbacks/buffers for incompatible uses. There are 275 parcels that
contain a P zoning either exclusively or within the parcel. The P zoning primarily prohibits
construction of a building; however, 43 existing sites contain structures.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The request consists of Zoning Text Amendment No. 2023-01 to amend various sections
of Title 17 of the NMC as it relates to the P zone and Zone Change No. 2023-01 to remove
the P zone from the zoning map.

The proposed update will simplify the list of permitted land uses and zones, minimize
conflicts between zoning code requirements, and serve as a proactive approach of
enhancing economic development.

ANALYSIS

A key objective of the proposed project is to expand development opportunities
throughout the city. The project will allow property owners to build on respective parcels,
while still conforming to requirements such as setbacks and building height. Additionally,
it will remove redundant provisions that are outdated from current conditions and that
conflict with goals to increase economic development. Recently approved projects, such
as the Alondra-Maidstone mixed-use development and the Rosecrans-Norwalk
commercial building are examples of vacant sites that remained dormant for a long time
and were difficult to redevelop due to the P zone. Summarized below are proposed
changes to the Zoning Code and Zoning Map.

Zoning Text Amendment

To simplify the code, staff proposes to delete the Automobile Parking (P) zoning and
related provisions. The P zoning significantly hinders development, where other design
features and code standards can apply and allow for development in a responsible
manner. In consideration that the P zoning created a buffer between potential
incompatible development, a minimum five feet setback and maximum 35 feet building
height are imposed to provide protections to adjacent residential zones. New
development proposed to reduce the minimum setback or exceed the maximum building
height would be subject to review and approval of a conditional use permit.

Zone Change

Of the total 275 parcels that will be affected by the zone change, 52 parcels will completely
revert to either residential (41) or commercial (11) zoning to match the underlying General
Plan land use designation, and 223 parcels will remove the partial P zoning buffer, which
is 15 to 50 feet wide, and revert to the corresponding zoning. The 223 split zoned parcels
will be re-designated as follows: 34.08% (76 parcels) as residential, 40.77% (95 parcels)
as industrial, 20.18% (45 parcels) as commercial, and the remaining 3.14% (7 parcels)
as open space or specific plan. The ZC will encourage development by expanding
developable area on the sites and providing the property owner more development
opportunities. Consistency between the zoning map and General Plan land use map will
occur as a result of this proposed project.

Public Notification

Notice of this public hearing was published in The Norwalk Patriot and posted at the City’s
three designated posting sites and the City website on September 14, 2023. All 3,444
property owners within 300 feet of impacted parcels were also notified.

ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT

 The project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3). The project will not involve any construction nor
have a significant effect on the environment.

SUMMARY

The proposed ZTA and ZC involve removing the Automobile Parking zone and related
provisions from the Norwalk Municipal Code, and corresponding zone on the City Zoning
Map. With the amendments, development opportunities will expand consistent with the
General Plan, conflicts between zoning code requirements will be minimized, and the list
of permitted uses and zones will be simplified. Staff recommends that the Planning
Commission recommend approval of the project to City Council.

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

The Precise Development Plan (PDP) requirement was adopted by Ordinance No. 757
in 1972 and intended to achieve a reasonable level of quality in harmony with precise
plans and community objectives for social, economic and physical well-being, and to
protect existing and potential developments and uses on adjacent and surrounding
properties. A precise development plan involves a set of plans conforming to the zoning
code that is subject to review and approval by the Planning Commission. It does not grant
provisions to deny any use already permitted by the NMC nor grant an unpermitted use
in any zone. The application is prompted with new construction or the relocation of
structures in any zone other than single-family residences and accessory buildings in
residential zones.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The request consists of Zoning Text Amendment No. 2023-02 to amend various sections
of Title 17 of the NMC to streamline the PDP process. It will serve as a proactive approach
of enhancing economic development and encouraging a positive image of the City.

ANALYSIS

The project will expedite the PDP application by reducing the associated processing time
and changing the reviewing authority to the Community Development Director. With
PDPs, the review primarily involves checking site plans, floor plans, and elevations in
conformance with development standards in the NMC and ensuring compatibility with the
neighborhood. In converting to an administrative process, the PDP will encourage the
redevelopment of vacant properties, create more opportunities for employment and goods
and services, and promote a positive image of the development process in Norwalk. Even
with a streamlined process, the proposed amendment will allow the Community
Development Director to refer a project to the Planning Commission for discretionary
action. Additionally, if a PDP were submitted concurrently with a discretionary application,
such as a conditional use permit, both applications would be subject to review and
approval by the Planning Commission. Review by the Director will apply to projects that
are permitted in the zone, conform to development standards in the NMC, and solely
require a PDP.

Public Notification

Notice of this public hearing was published in The Norwalk Patriot and posted at the City’s
three designated posting sites and the City website on September 28, 2022.

17.02.205 Precise development plans.

A. Purpose and Intent. The purpose and intent of requiring precise development plan
review is to achieve a reasonable level of quality in harmony with precise plans and
community objectives for social, economic and physical well-being, and to protect
existing and potential developments and uses on adjacent and surrounding properties.

In order to achieve the purpose of this section, it is considered necessary to require that
the use of land, and erection, construction or location of buildings or structures in any
zone other than single-family residences and accessory buildings in the R-1, R-2, R-3,
and R-H zones, unless in conjunction with a new and/or proposed subdivision, shall
conform with approved development plans; and, further, that reasonable conditions may
be imposed to serve and protect public health, safety, necessity, convenience and
general welfare. No provision of this chapter is intended to deny any use already
permitted by this title nor to grant any use in a zone not therein authorized.

B. Applicability. The Community Development Director (Director) shall review
applications in accordance with 17.02.105 Review Authority Table, as well as the
following development and use applications:

1.  The erection or construction of a building; or

2. The moving of a building onto property, or the relocation of a building or substantial
structure from one part of a property to another.

C. General Procedures. The Director shall prescribe the form of application,
documents to be submitted and the type of information to be provided by the applicant.
No application shall be accepted for filing unless it complies with the requirements set
forth.

1. Application for precise development plan review shall be filed prior to issuance of
building permits and shall be accompanied by detailed and fully dimensioned building
plans, architectural drawings and elevations, landscape plans and/or any other data
found to be reasonably required, and shall include the following:

a. The size, shape, height, orientation and location of all existing and proposed
buildings; floor plans; the type and color of exterior materials proposed;

b.  The size, spacing and location of all doors, windows and other openings;

structures;

f.  The location, height, and materials to be used in construction of walls and fences;

g.  The landscaping and irrigation plan proposed;

h. Any other feature of development, which may have a significant impact upon or

Article IV Administrative Approvals and Permits

17.02.205 Precise development plans.

A. Purpose and Intent. The purpose and intent of requiring precise development plan
review is to achieve a reasonable level of quality in harmony with precise plans and
community objectives for social, economic and physical well-being, and to protect
existing and potential developments and uses on adjacent and surrounding properties.

In order to achieve the purpose of this section, it is considered necessary to require that
the use of land, and erection, construction or location of buildings or structures in any
zone other than single-family residences and accessory buildings in the R-1, R-2, R-3,
and R-H zones, unless in conjunction with a new and/or proposed subdivision, shall
conform with approved development plans; and, further, that reasonable conditions may
be imposed to serve and protect public health, safety, necessity, convenience and
general welfare. No provision of this chapter is intended to deny any use already
permitted by this title nor to grant any use in a zone not therein authorized.

B. Applicability. The Community Development Director (Director) shall review
applications in accordance with 17.02.105 Review Authority Table, as well as the
following development and use applications:

1.  The erection or construction of a building; or

2. The moving of a building onto property, or the relocation of a building or substantial
structure from one part of a property to another.

C. General Procedures. The Director shall prescribe the form of application,
documents to be submitted and the type of information to be provided by the applicant.
No application shall be accepted for filing unless it complies with the requirements set
forth.

1. Application for precise development plan review shall be filed prior to issuance of
building permits and shall be accompanied by detailed and fully dimensioned building
plans, architectural drawings and elevations, landscape plans and/or any other data
found to be reasonably required, and shall include the following:

a. The size, shape, height, orientation and location of all existing and proposed
buildings; floor plans; the type and color of exterior materials proposed;

 b.  The size, spacing and location of all doors, windows and other openings;

c. The type and pitch of roofs, towers, chimneys and other roof or architectural
structures;

d. The location, number and size of parking spaces, driveways and other factors
affecting required off-street parking;

e.  The location and type of lighting for buildings, grounds and parking areas;

f.  The location, height, and materials to be used in construction of walls and fences;

g.  The landscaping and irrigation plan proposed;

h. Any other feature of development, which may have a significant impact upon or
relationship to existing and/or proposed development in such area.

2. Precise development plans shall be filed for review and acted upon concurrently
with an application for a change of zone, except that:

a. The Director may defer presentation of all or a part of required precise
development plans to the building permit stage if it determines that the size, nature, or
complexity of development is such as may necessitate significant revisions and that
preliminary plans filed are of sufficient detail to establish general compliance with the
purpose and intent of this chapter.

b. In the event of a change of zone initiated by the Planning Commission or City
Council, pursuant to Section 17.02.290, compliance with this section shall be required
prior to issuance of building permits.

3. Any precise development plan located within the PF zone shall be reviewed by the
Community Development Director.

D.  Standards and Review Criteria.

1. The Community Development Director may at his or her discretion refer any
request to the Planning Commission for review. The Community Development Director
shall determine whether the proposed development is in compliance with regulations of
this code and provisions of this section, and whether or not such development will be
detrimental to the public health, safety and welfare or adversely affect property values
or the present and future development of surrounding areas. Consideration shall be
given to building orientation, walls or fences, landscaping, general design
and development, setbacks, height, vehicular and pedestrian ingress and egress,
parking, lighting, and the relationship of such factors to existing and
proposed development in the immediate and surrounding area.

 2. The Director, in compliance with the foregoing, may recommend approval, or
conditional approval subject to modifications, of any precise development plan. The
following findings may endanger the public health, safety, convenience and welfare and
may be cause for denial of a precise development plan:

The proposed development would substantially depreciate property values in the vicinity
or interfere with the use or enjoyment of property in such area, because of excessive
dissimilarity or in appropriateness of design in relation to the surrounding vicinity.

3. The Director may require modification in the architectural treatment of buildings or
structures, require additional landscaping or development improvements and
reasonably impose such other conditions as are deemed necessary, in its judgment, to
insure compliance with regulations and the purpose, spirit and intent of this code, and
thereby serve the best interest of the area and community.

E.  Decision, Transmittal, Appeal.

1. The Director shall deliver or mail by first class mail a notice of its decision,
approving or denying a precise development plan, to the Planning Commission and
applicant.

2. The decision of the Director shall become final and effective ten (10) calendar days
after the delivery or mailing of all notices required by this section unless prior to 5:00
p.m. of the 10th day, either of the following has occurred:

a. A written appeal has been filed with the Community Development Department by
an applicant or by a person specially aggrieved, and accompanied by the payment of a
fee per any applicable fee resolution adopted by City Council; or

b.  The Planning Commission elects to review the decision of the Director.

3. The decision of the Planning Commission may be appealed to the City Council
within ten (10) calendar days after the date that notice of the decision is mailed to the
applicant. Notice of the appeal, and of the appeal hearing before the City Council, shall
be pursuant to the hearing and noticing requirements contained in Sections
17.02.050.A.4 and 17.02.090.F.

F.  Compliance.

1. An approved plan shall be valid for a one-year period and, should development fail
to commence within such time limitation and no extension is granted therefore, shall
become null and void.

2. No person shall violate or fail to comply with any approved plan or any condition or
provision thereof, nor shall a building permit be issued for any building or structure
